symptoms: Yellowing and drooping of leaves on one side of the plant or one branch first
Brown streaks visible inside the stem when split lengthwise
Plants wilt suddenly in patches, often after irrigation
Stunted plants with browning vascular ring; leaf edges scorch

severity_cues.early: Isolated wilting plants in a patch
severity_cues.advanced: Patch-wise plant death across the field

favorable_conditions: Warm moist soil, poor drainage, nematode-damaged roots, continuous cotton cropping

treatment.summary: No chemical cures a wilted plant. Save the rest of the field: sanitation, biologicals, drainage, rotation
steps: Uproot and destroy wilted plants with root soil, burn or bury them away from the field
Treat seed for next sowing with Trichoderma viride at 4 to 6 g per kg seed
Plan a 2 to 3 year rotation with non-host crops such as sorghum or maize
Manage root-knot nematodes, they open the door for Fusarium
organic: Trichoderma viride or harzianum: seed treatment 4 to 6 g per kg, and soil application with FYM
Neem cake application to soil at recommended rates

source.org: ICAR Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), cotton disease advisory
source.title: Cotton: wilt management

safety_notes: No spray is involved: safety comes from sanitation and rotation discipline
Wilted plants must be removed with root soil, never left to dry in the field
